author: keiretsu
cardQuote: Let's face it, Youtube, Facebook are all toys. They have eyeballs but no scalable business model.
quote: I have yet to see any true ipo-able web business to appear so far. When i mean truly ipo-able, i mean it has a REAL business model and one that can scale to billions. Something like Paypal or Ebay. Let's face it, Youtube, Facebook are all toys. They have eyeballs but no scalable business model. The best hope i've seen so far is Prosper.com. It doesn't have the massive eyeballs yet but hey, at least their biz model is scalable. Does this mean that all the good billion-dollar ipo-able web ideas have been taken up? Is this it?
storyTitle: Web 2.0 is more about toys than anything
outcome: 2B+ monthly logged-in users; a core part of Google's ad business.
outcomeDetail: YouTube turned free video into a massive advertising business, paid billions of dollars to creators, and became the default video platform. It passed 2 billion monthly logged-in users and remains central to Google's revenue.
note: The critique was right that eyeballs alone are not a business. YouTube's scale, targeting, and creator ecosystem turned those eyeballs into one.

author: bmaier
cardQuote: Twitter is a nice fringe communication tool but simply that.
quote: Personally, I don't think anything will truly replace email (at least not for many many years). Twitter is a nice fringe communication tool but simply that. Hopefully what Twitter and the new communication apps will contribute to is a reduction in the number of pointless short emails I get. Perhaps the article should be titled, Twitter is the new IM.
storyTitle: Scoble: Twitter etc are the next email
outcome: IPO in 2013; sold to Elon Musk for $44B in 2022.
outcomeDetail: Twitter became a global real-time network with hundreds of millions of users, went public in 2013, and was acquired by Elon Musk in 2022 in a $44 billion deal. It did not replace email, but it became far more than a fringe tool.
note: The email-replacement framing came from the article, not Twitter. Twitter became a primary news and communication channel, though its business stayed volatile.

author: mattmccor
cardQuote: If you don't think Facebook is a fad, ask if you can really see Facebook being around in 20 years. I certaintly can't.
quote: If you don't think Facebook is a fad, ask if you can really see Facebook being around in 20 years. I certaintly can't. It is a fad, just one that may take some time to run out.
storyTitle: Fadnation: Why Steve Ballmer Could Be Right
outcome: 3B+ monthly users across Meta's apps; a trillion-dollar company.
outcomeDetail: Facebook kept growing for two decades, bought Instagram and WhatsApp, and became Meta. Its family of apps reaches more than 3 billion monthly users, and the advertising business made it one of the world's most valuable companies.
note: The 20-year horizon was the test, and Facebook passed it. It evolved from a college network into an advertising and messaging empire.

author: jimboyoungblood
cardQuote: Wave is more confusing than it is inspirational. My first thought upon opening the invite was "wtf?", and after a few minutes of staring at it, "wtf?!?".
quote: Perhaps it does. But if it did, I think we'd be seeing articles like "How I used Google Wave to get laid and make money", not speculative "What could Wave be possibly useful for?" articles like this one. Wave is more confusing than it is inspirational. My first thought upon opening the invite was "wtf?", and after a few minutes of staring at it, "wtf?!?". Then I closed the window. Maybe wave will become useful after a few iterations, but in its current incarnation it's in the same category as Yahoo Pipes. I.e., technically interesting/dazzling, but of little practical use.
storyTitle: Google Wave's Best Use Cases
outcome: Development stopped in 2010; service shut down in 2012.
outcomeDetail: Google stopped development of Wave in August 2010 and shut the service down in 2012. Its ideas influenced later collaboration tools, but the product never found a mainstream use case.
note: The "what is this for?" problem was fatal. Wave's protocol ambition outran its interface and its audience.

author: waterlesscloud
cardQuote: Migration of my friends to FB email seems far more likely to me than migration of all my social graph to Google Buzz.
quote: Which assumes people don't move to Facebook email. Migration of my friends to FB email seems far more likely to me than migration of all my social graph to Google Buzz. It would also be trivial for FB to allow response to notifications via external email if they decide to do it. I think people are seriously underestimating the value of Facebook's existing graphs. They've been shaped over a couple of years now to what most people want them to be. The vast majority are not going to leave that behind for a me-too service.
storyTitle: Google Buzz
outcome: Discontinued in 2011 after a privacy backlash.
outcomeDetail: Buzz launched inside Gmail, auto-followed contacts, and triggered a privacy outcry. Google added controls, then discontinued Buzz in 2011. It was a major social failure for Google before Google+.
note: The Facebook graph was the moat. Buzz's Gmail integration could not overcome it, and the product was gone within two years.

author: Brizz
cardQuote: This is an app built by engineers in the valley for engineers in the valley. This "bubble" project is truly a bubble.
quote: This is an app built by engineers in the valley for engineers in the valley. This "bubble" project is truly a bubble. You need to step outside your own experience and understand if your products are viable to others who aren't you. Walk around anywhere that's not SF or NY and this app will be useless for at least the first year. And who can can make sense of this UI other than an engineer? Engineering breakthrough? Yes. Useful mobile tool? No.
storyTitle: Sequoia gives photo-sharing startup more money than they gave Google
outcome: Pivoted, then sold its team to Apple for a reported $7M in 2012.
outcomeDetail: Color raised $41 million before launch, stumbled with a confusing proximity-photo app, pivoted, and sold its engineering team to Apple in 2012 for a reported $7 million. The product shut down.
note: The "engineers building for engineers" critique nailed the product's insulation from normal users. The $41 million launch became a bubble shorthand.

author: merloen
cardQuote: So I have doubts about the quality of the translations, and I have doubts about how they're planning to merge translations from different users, which sounds like a very tricky problem.
quote: Interesting, but I'm skeptical. I studied translation, and noticed to my surprise that the foreign language part of translating is fairly easy, unless it's highly technical, or contains dialect or slang. The hard part was the command of my native language. I was pretty literate, but the translations I produced weren't good enough - they were accurate, but wooden, and they stayed too close to the original. What I had to learn was my own native language. So I have doubts about the quality of the translations, and I have doubts about how they're planning to merge translations from different users, which sounds like a very tricky problem. And it looks like the only exercise they use is to translate the foreign language (e.g. Spanish) into the native language, which will teach you to read, but not to write, speak or understand Spanish. Nevertheless, a fascinating experiment, and an extremely ingenious idea.
storyTitle: The scoop on reCAPTCHA founder's new startup Duolingo.
outcome: IPO in 2021; 100M+ monthly learners.
outcomeDetail: Duolingo turned lessons into a mass-market app, went public in 2021, and grew past 100 million monthly active users. Its crowdsourced translation business faded, but language learning became a durable consumer subscription.
note: The translation-quality doubt was fair, but Duolingo's real product became language learning, not translation. The critique judged the wrong business.

author: kmgroove
cardQuote: The market is small, the market is tiny. It only seems large because of the internet. In reality the market for spectator e-sports is very small (and beyond star craft it is pretty much non-existent).
quote: You mean in one place that offers very little (if any?) real sport competition? More people in Korea would be watching a successful South Korean soccer team then even the biggest of star craft 2 events. The market is small, the market is tiny. It only seems large because of the internet. In reality the market for spectator e-sports is very small (and beyond star craft it is pretty much non-existent). The only way e-sports will ever become a profitable market beyond niche is to engage it at the casual player with accessible leagues/ladders/ and tournaments for all. Blizzard kind of does it but they don't provide a good interface for it in my opinion. All others who try have failed pretty hard. Beyond sc2 e-sports have been declining and failing left right and center. And absolutely nothing that I see coming from game companies give me faith that this will change. Star craft 2 is a nice niche but it does not represent the e-sports market as a whole. That market is tiny, and largely ignored and at the current time requires real innovation. In my opinion the real money in e-sports (when it finally does get big) will not be spectating at all, it will come from little Johny paying 5$ a month to play in a very well run, exiting, competitive and fun casual league. Someone just needs to build it right.
storyTitle: Justin.tv launches TwitchTV: A destination site for eSports
outcome: Acquired by Amazon for $970M in 2014; now the leading game-streaming service.
outcomeDetail: Twitch became the dominant live-streaming platform for games and a major creator economy. Amazon bought it for $970 million in 2014, and it remains central to game streaming and esports.
note: The critique assumed esports had to look like traditional sports. Twitch's audience was bigger, younger, and global; the niche became a platform.

author: dendory
cardQuote: I dislike Facebook like anybody, but this will not take off any more than Buzz or Wave I'm afraid.
quote: I dislike Facebook like anybody, but this will not take off any more than Buzz or Wave I'm afraid. This will be that side thing that people may or may not notice when they search. This isn't the site people will flock to when they wake up to see what their friends have been doing.
storyTitle: Google Reveals Its Stealth Social Project, Google+
outcome: Consumer Google+ shut down in 2019.
outcomeDetail: Google+ reached hundreds of millions of registered users but never became a daily habit. Google announced its consumer shutdown in 2018 after a data exposure and closed it in 2019.
note: The Buzz and Wave comparison was the right prior. Google could ship social features, but it could not make social graphs feel native.

author: blocke
cardQuote: Could someone please tell me why people are excited about Spotify in the US? We have established competitors and I've failed to find a single thing Spotify does better than the competitors.
quote: Could someone please tell me why people are excited about Spotify in the US? We have established competitors and I've failed to find a single thing Spotify does better than the competitors. Also the competitors do this amazing thing that Spotify doesn't: They work in a web browser.
storyTitle: Spotify launches in the US
outcome: 600M+ users; public since 2018.
outcomeDetail: Spotify expanded from Europe to the U.S., survived the licensing gauntlet, and became the world's largest audio streaming service. It went public via a direct listing in 2018 and passed 600 million monthly users.
note: The browser complaint missed the point: Spotify's desktop app, playlists, and catalog made it the default. The competitors were not as integrated.

author: joshklein
cardQuote: The question for reddit isn't whether or not people enjoy it and want to spend time on it, but whether or not the owners can make money selling those people's attention.
quote: The question for reddit isn't whether or not people enjoy it and want to spend time on it, but whether or not the owners can make money selling those people's attention. The traffic to reddit - while admirably large - is relatively unattractive to most advertisers. "Reach" (impressions/eyeballs) are only important insofar as you're talking to someone who might buy what you're selling (see "relevancy"). The sub-reddit system could theoretically segment the audience in interesting ways, but other than r/gaming, there aren't many natural industry fits amongst popular sub-reddits. Anecdotally, the audience would also seem to be advertisement-averse. An advertiser should be willing to pay network prices for the audience (i.e. pennies CPM), which makes it a nice living for a small group of folks living off their passion, but pretty useless to a Condé Nast trying to run a media empire. I think the business model in a reddit-like site could be selling curated content in other media, e.g. a meme-series of coffee table books. Think Harry Potter, not Oprah. If you're in the content game, your business's value is in having the attention of a group of people. Your first attempt to monetize that asset needn't be to sell your audience's attention to someone else, in this case undermining your ability to keep their attention. Instead, you should focus on bringing things your audience wants - and would pay for - to them. Sometimes that means you need to make the things they want to buy instead of shilling them for someone else, because no one sells what your people want. Condé Nast isn't built to do this.
storyTitle: Reddit becomes reddit Inc.
outcome: IPO in 2024; 100M+ daily active users.
outcomeDetail: Reddit grew into a major advertising platform, went public in March 2024, and reported more than 100 million daily active users. Its niche communities turned out to be valuable to advertisers after all.
note: The ad-aversion concern was real, but Reddit's scale, targeting, and search data made the model work. The critique underestimated how much advertisers would pay for niche communities.

author: cmelbye
cardQuote: Is it bad that I've never heard of this app or seen it been used in the wild before? The iPhone app looks really ugly, and I can't see myself convincing my friends to start using it if they have to pay for the app when we could just be using iMessage, SMS, or Facebook Messenger.
quote: Is it bad that I've never heard of this app or seen it been used in the wild before? The iPhone app looks really ugly, and I can't see myself convincing my friends to start using it if they have to pay for the app when we could just be using iMessage, SMS, or Facebook Messenger. What's the draw here?
storyTitle: WhatsApp bucks convention, quietly builds a messaging titan
outcome: Acquired by Facebook for $19B in 2014; 2B+ users.
outcomeDetail: WhatsApp became the default messaging app in much of the world, was bought by Facebook for $19 billion in 2014, and passed 2 billion users. Its phone-number graph and cross-platform simplicity beat the free alternatives.
note: The "what's the draw" question had an answer: address-book identity and cross-platform messaging. The ugly-app critique aged badly too.

author: notatoad
cardQuote: i think we can confidently say that it's a fad. social content aggregators don't last. it's just a fact of the industry.
quote: >But, Pinterest is so new (relatively), we don't really know whether it's just a fad or something to stay i think we can confidently say that it's a fad. social content aggregators don't last. it's just a fact of the industry. kudos to pinterest for collecting some cash while they're hot, but it's only a matter of time before they go the same way as all their predecessors.
storyTitle: Pinterest Raises $100 MM at $1.5Bn Valuation
outcome: IPO in 2019; 500M+ monthly users.
outcomeDetail: Pinterest went public in 2019 and grew into a visual search and shopping company with more than 500 million monthly users. It became profitable and remains one of the largest social platforms.
note: "Social content aggregators don't last" was a strong rule until Pinterest outlasted several. Its shopping intent made it unusually durable.

author: anon808
cardQuote: google glass reminds me of the segway . . . really cool futuristic idea that just doesn't fit with the way life is lived.
quote: google glass reminds me of the segway . . . really cool futuristic idea that just doesn't fit with the way life is lived.
storyTitle: Sergey Brin Demos Google Glass At I/O
outcome: Consumer Explorer program ended in 2015; enterprise version discontinued in 2023.
outcomeDetail: Google stopped selling the consumer Explorer edition in 2015 after privacy backlash and weak demand. An enterprise version lingered, but Google discontinued Glass for enterprise in 2023.
note: The Segway comparison captured the social awkwardness and the use-case gap. Glass was a demo looking for a place in daily life.

author: Lewisham
cardQuote: My wild guess is that they still give people headaches as with previous VR attempts, and no-one is willing to put money in the pot with the expectation that it is unsolvable.
quote: The video sets off all sorts of alarm bells. Something about this is very, very wrong. Why would all these game developers agree to be in a video endorsing the product, but not actually front money for it? iD/Zenimax, Epic and Valve would all see the hoped for $250 000 as chump change for a dev kit. Split between the three and it's essentially nothing. My guess is Microsoft or Sony would love nothing more than to tie up an exclusive peripheral for their next-gen consoles, and buy the company outright (as MS did with Kinect). This would be a true differentiator. That they're looking to Kickstarter to sell $300 dev kits makes me think something very bad is going unsaid. My wild guess is that they still give people headaches as with previous VR attempts, and no-one is willing to put money in the pot with the expectation that it is unsolvable. People putting money into this are as crazy as those who put money into the OUYA.
storyTitle: Oculus Rift: Step Into the Game
outcome: Acquired by Facebook for $2B in 2014; Quest headsets sold millions.
outcomeDetail: Oculus shipped developer kits, was acquired by Facebook for $2 billion in 2014, and eventually produced the Quest line of standalone VR headsets. Consumer VR stayed niche, but Oculus built a real hardware business.
note: The nausea and hype concerns were real. The conclusion that no one would fund it was wrong: Facebook bought the company two years later.

author: vubuntu
cardQuote: Just a novelty that will fade off. I cant see any useful purpose for 6 second clips in a social wide audience context.
quote: Thank god there is another sane person like me. I too find it difficult to make sense or enjoy just 6 second snippets. Conveying a sweet short targeted message for a specific someone with just a 6 second video itself is so hard, let alone be able to generate a 6 second content that is of meaning/relevance to a much broader audience. Just a novelty that will fade off. I cant see any useful purpose for 6 second clips in a social wide audience context.
storyTitle: Show HN: Vinepeek - watch the world in realtime in 6 second snippets
outcome: Shut down in 2017 after Twitter stopped supporting it.
outcomeDetail: Vine grew to hundreds of millions of users and created a short-video vocabulary, but Twitter never built a durable business around it. Twitter shut Vine down in 2017.
note: Vine was a genuine cultural phenomenon, so "novelty" was too dismissive in the short run. The six-second format and the company did not last.

author: inflatablenerd
cardQuote: For most people, Path doesn't offer anything they don't get from Facebook, or Twitter, or Foursquare, or Instagram, so they stop posting or checking the app.
quote: I don't think being mobile only is Path's problem. Plenty of social networks like Instagram and WhatsApp have flourished without a webpage. For most people, Path doesn't offer anything they don't get from Facebook, or Twitter, or Foursquare, or Instagram, so they stop posting or checking the app.
storyTitle: Path 3 is out
outcome: Shut down in October 2018.
outcomeDetail: Path raised venture money and shipped polished apps, but it never escaped Facebook's shadow. The company shut the social network down in October 2018.
note: The differentiation problem was the real one. Path's privacy-first design was not enough to overcome the network effect of the incumbents.

author: jimkri
cardQuote: As a college student I think the app is stupid. They will need a total change in the future, because at certain points all the app contains is posts that are just copied over from the top list, Reddit, or some other site.
quote: As a college student I think the app is stupid. They will need a total change in the future, because at certain points all the app contains is posts that are just copied over from the top list, Reddit, or some other site. There is nothing interesting. Most of the people who use the app just want to be recognized as being funny or edgy, their up vote is what people have bragged to me about.
storyTitle: The inside story of Yik Yak
outcome: Shut down in 2017; its team joined Square.
outcomeDetail: Yik Yak raised $73 million and peaked on college campuses, but harassment and moderation problems followed it. The company shut down in 2017, and Square hired its team.
note: The "nothing interesting" problem was real: without fresh local content, the feed became a loop of screenshots and inside jokes. The app shut down in 2017.

author: xlm1717
cardQuote: Tinder/Grindr are fads that are already fading.
quote: Whatsapp and Instagram were acquired by Facebook and Vine was acquired by Twitter. Tinder/Grindr are fads that are already fading. Snapchat, it's probably a matter of time before they get acquired or people get bored with it.
storyTitle: Ask HN: Do you think we'll see any Twitter/Facebook real-competitor?
outcome: 75M monthly users and 9M paying subscribers by 2025.
outcomeDetail: Tinder became the anchor of Match Group's dating portfolio, with 75 million monthly active users, 9 million paying users, and $1.86 billion in revenue in 2025. It did not fade; it defined mobile dating.
note: The "fad" call confused a new interface with a short shelf life. Tinder's swipe model became the default.

author: coldtea
cardQuote: No. Nobody cares that much for their friends (especially their hundreds of "friends" on social media), or has that time to spare on real-time streaming.
quote: > Can private broadcasting succeed where public live-streaming failed? No. Nobody cares that much for their friends (especially their hundreds of "friends" on social media), or has that time to spare on real-time streaming. For the times when this is actually needed, there are tons of videoconference apps. Next question?
storyTitle: Meerkat built a new app under a pseudonym, and almost 1M people are using it
outcome: Epic acquired it in 2019 and shut it down in 2021.
outcomeDetail: Houseparty became a pandemic-era hit in 2020, but its growth did not last. Epic Games, which bought the company in 2019, shut Houseparty down in October 2021.
note: Houseparty briefly proved the critic wrong during lockdown. As a standalone product, though, it could not outlast the video-call features built into everything else.

author: pavanlimo
cardQuote: But for the usecases it serves, it's probably enough. Not an expert in this domain but I'm struggling to see its value at $1B.
quote: I just gave it a go and it didn't really look like a Photoshop replacement, more like a really trimmed version of Photoshop. But for the usecases it serves, it's probably enough. Not an expert in this domain but I'm struggling to see its value at $1B. May be the community is high quality and large?
storyTitle: Canva becomes Australia’s only privately backed tech startup to be valued at $1B
outcome: Valued at $32B in 2024; 220M monthly users.
outcomeDetail: Canva kept adding templates, collaboration, video, and AI tools, and its valuation climbed to $32 billion in 2024. It serves more than 200 million monthly users and is one of the most valuable private software companies.
note: The "trimmed Photoshop" framing missed the market: non-designers wanted templates and collaboration, not a full editor.

author: jariel
cardQuote: To boot, TikTok is a fad. It's just a bigger vine, and teenager will quickly move on to something more substantial over time.
quote: This will be Nadella's Albatross. He's been given far too much credit for being a 'nice guy' whilst most operationalising the foundations left for him. He has not done anything fundamental for the company, other than changed the tone of the leadership of the company. He's a good steward. TikTok is completely out of MS cultural reach, and in that way it's a poor fit. Remember Skype? How about IE that ruled the world and MS couldn't figure it out either. To boot, TikTok is a fad. It's just a bigger vine, and teenager will quickly move on to something more substantial over time. FB is truly a social network and has a degree of lock-in and therefore staying power, but younger people have largely fled it as well. Snapchat and Twitter both have baseline utility for communicating. I'm not sure TikTok is any of that - it has the faddish appeal, but none of the underlying utility.
storyTitle: TikTok’s potential $588 per user valuation in Microsoft deal
outcome: 1B+ monthly users; one of the world's largest apps.
outcomeDetail: TikTok kept growing through the Microsoft-Oracle sale saga, passed a billion monthly users, and became the most-downloaded app in the world. It is now a primary cultural and advertising platform.
note: "Bigger Vine" underestimated the algorithmic feed and global scale. TikTok did not stay a teen fad.

author: t_serpico
cardQuote: Because of COVID, people turn to CH to replicate this experience. After COVID, I suspect this app will die out.
quote: The question is why would you gossip on CH? My guess is that there is some excitement to 'getting caught' or just more generally doing it in public. It's like the equivalent of having a private conversation in a bar or coffee shop. Because of COVID, people turn to CH to replicate this experience. After COVID, I suspect this app will die out.
storyTitle: Clubhouse’s Inevitability
outcome: Downloads collapsed after the pandemic; staff were cut in 2022.
outcomeDetail: Clubhouse peaked during lockdown, raised at a $4 billion valuation, and then lost most of its momentum. Downloads fell more than 80% year over year in 2022, and the company laid off staff as it pivoted to smaller private groups.
note: The pandemic-dependence critique was right. Clubhouse's invite-only, live-only format did not survive the return of in-person life and copycat features from bigger platforms.

author: exreddit
cardQuote: I doubt there's much value here to squeeze. People lose interest in these things pretty fast.
quote: I still can't get over that I looked at the morning's news, saw something about this, recognized the same, and was like "I know that guy!" Congrats on the viral hit and all the free press. Josh is a great guy. I doubt there's much value here to squeeze. People lose interest in these things pretty fast. By the time it's productionized, it might be too late, and it ruined a fun hobby. The big value is he has a platform to launch something else, or enough attention to land a pretty good next gig.
storyTitle: Ask HN: What do you think of the Wordle guy not monetizing it?
outcome: Sold to the New York Times in 2022; still a daily habit.
outcomeDetail: The New York Times bought Wordle for a low seven-figure sum in early 2022, and the game remained one of the most-played daily puzzles on the web. It did not disappear after the viral moment.
note: The prediction was about monetization, not the game's durability. Wordle's simple daily ritual outlasted the hype cycle.
